Yes. The latest analysis detected **13.5 hectares of tree-cover loss in 2025**, about 3.9% of the property. The JRC 2020 reference classified 98% of the affected area as forest.

The event has not yet met the tool’s corroboration rule, which requires observation of a later year; 2025 is the latest year available. Tree-cover loss also does not necessarily mean permanent deforestation.
